text.en: Eight-year-old Valli wants to ride a bus. Today we follow her adventure.

Valli is eight years old and very curious. She likes to stand at the front door and watch the street.
The most fascinating thing is the bus that goes between her village and the nearest town. It passes her street every hour.
She longs to ride the bus even once, but friends who have ridden it make her jealous, and she calls them proud.
She listens to conversations and finds out the details: the town is six miles away, the fare is thirty paise one way, and the trip takes forty-five minutes.
She plans to take the one o'clock bus, stay on it, and come back home on the same bus by about a quarter to three.
She saves her coins and finally travels, sitting by the window, feeling grown-up and proud of herself.
The story is told with humour. It shows a child's curiosity, planning, courage and wish for independence.
It is translated from Tamil by K. S. Sundaram and illustrated by R. K. Laxman.
